{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ks-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"c9e13f615726d43b5964d8b420bbd4a53c5f1a06230d8810f207400c577ac344","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ks-class-c:lineage:36","source_registry_sha256":"c7fb2073a9e8bb6a73d0151458fe04991b703d84f882b00a01bedfcea433c383","source_liveness_sha256":"94328be42cc10cf86af8e486b41bc40c72c45e4700d27b9b46d1f3d2feac7bb6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Collision avoidance and emergencies","heading":"C — Collision avoidance and emergencies","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Collision avoidance and emergencies

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A73
Collision-avoidance responses include braking, steering or accelerating, depending on available space and the threat. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A73
Read the vehicle owner's manual for its ABS instructions. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A73
For a rapid stop with ABS, press the brake firmly and keep pressure on it. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A73
ABS operation may push back through the brake pedal; maintain pressure rather than lifting because of that feedback. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A73
Without ABS, overly hard braking can lock the wheels and start a skid. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A73
For a rapid stop without ABS, apply as much braking as possible without locking the wheels. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A73
If non-ABS brakes lock, ease pedal pressure without removing the foot, then reapply controlled braking once the skid ends. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A73
Repeat non-ABS release-and-reapply control as needed until stopped. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A73
Steering around a collision threat may be quicker than stopping in many situations. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A73
Keep both hands firmly on the wheel during emergency steering and remain ready to control the vehicle after the avoidance move. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A73
Steer toward the intended path and avoid escaping one collision into another. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A73
A seat belt helps keep the driver in position behind the wheel during an emergency maneuver. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A73
With ABS during an emergency steering maneuver, maintain firm brake pressure while steering toward the intended path. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A73
Without ABS, avoid hard braking while steering if possible; stronger braking can resume after reaching the intended path and straightening. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A73
Acceleration may avoid a side or rear strike when open space exists ahead; slow again after the danger passes. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A74
Wet, snowy or icy surfaces, excessive speed and abrupt stopping can cause tires to lose their grip. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A74
At the start of traction loss, look toward available open space rather than fixating on the hazard. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A74
The handbook's skid-identification step releases accelerator or brake pressure to help determine whether front or rear traction is lost. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A74
If steering does not change the vehicle's straight path, the front tires have lost traction. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A74
Sideways movement without added steering input indicates rear-tire traction loss. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A74
For front traction loss in the described non-ABS response, ease braking to recover grip and reapply without skidding. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A74
For front traction loss with ABS, the handbook directs full brake application to regain steering control. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A74
For rear traction loss, steer toward the desired path and countersteer as needed until straight, continuing to look toward that path. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A74
During skid recovery, avoid looking into the opposing lane because the vehicle may follow that gaze across the centerline. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A74
With traction-assistance technology during rear traction loss, keep steering toward the desired path to assist the system. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A74
If a collision cannot be avoided, seat-belt use is a key way to reduce resulting injury. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A74
For a rear impact, press against the seat back with the head against its restraint and prepare to brake against being pushed into another vehicle. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A74
Lap-and-shoulder belts help retain the driver behind the wheel in a side impact; prepare to steer or brake to avoid a subsequent collision. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A74
Seat belts help protect and retain the driver if a frontal crash is followed by another collision. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0074]

Misconceptions: ABS hard-stop technique differs from non-ABS lockup recovery and from actual brake failure. A tire blowout calls for gradual slowing; visibility advice does not guarantee a speed is safe.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: identify the failure, preserve control, find space, stop safely. It adds no equipment instruction.
Glossary: Separate front traction loss, rear traction loss, brake failure, tire blowout, engine shutdown, accelerator failure and pavement drop-off using their source-bound conditions.
Dynamic facts: Vehicle controls, airbags and traction systems depend on equipment documentation; numerical risk and stopping claims with missing assumptions remain typed debt. The edition's procedures require issuer refresh before replacing this source.
